title: Extending the identity-coordinate transpose across an equivariant monomorphism
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group, with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Use internal $A$-modules, internal $G$-actions, their forgetful functor $U$, and section modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For a profinite parameter $X$, let $A[\underline X]$ be the free internal module, left adjoint to forgetting to condensed sets, with canonical local generators $[t]$ [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]. Use internal tensor and its right-adjoint internal Hom [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], whose sections are maps on the entire slice [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Fix $n\geq0$ and an equivariant module $J$. Put $P_n=A[\underline G^n]$, with $G^0=*$, and $\mathcal H_n(J)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{n+1}],UJ)$. A normalized homogeneous-function model means an equivariant module identified underneath with $\mathcal H_n(J)$ and having action $(k\cdot f)(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=k\cdot_J f(k^{-1}g_0,\ldots,k^{-1}g_n)$ on every profinite slice [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions].
Assume that $UJ$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $H$ be any normalized homogeneous-function model. Let $i:N\hookrightarrow M$ be a monomorphism in the internal equivariant module category and $h:N\to H$ an equivariant $A$-linear map. Then $P_n\otimes_A Ui$ is a monomorphism of internal modules. There is a unique internal $A$-linear map $\alpha:P_n\otimes_A UN\to UJ$ such that, for every profinite $S$, tuple $\mathbf t\in C(S,G)^n$, and $x\in N(S)$,
$$\alpha_S([\mathbf t]\otimes x)=h_S(x)(1,\mathbf t).$$
There exists an internal $A$-linear map $\beta:P_n\otimes_A UM\to UJ$ with $\beta\circ(P_n\otimes_A Ui)=\alpha$. Consequently, on every profinite test and after every base change,
$$\beta_S([\mathbf t]\otimes i_S(x))=h_S(x)(1,\mathbf t).$$
Here each tensor of local sections denotes its canonical image in the sheaf tensor, and each evaluation is the evaluation of the appropriate slice morphism. No injectivity of $J(S)$, projectivity of $P_n$, discreteness of $J$, or finiteness of $G$ is assumed.

Step 2: the evaluation in def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions, the slice Hom of def-pur-sheaf-hom, and the natural-assignment uniqueness and generator detection of free-linearization give b with naturality and A-linearity; it is correctly marked elementary. Step 3: lem-pe gives the pure-tensor comparison and lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed gives Hom(P_n⊗UN,UJ)≅Hom(UN,Hom(P_n,UJ)) in the right order. The formula is read through the canonical Stacks 03EO bijection, which is the same node the item's statement uses to define internal Hom, so I accept it. Uniqueness follows from generator detection on every T→S. Step 4 uses only injectivity of UJ (def-sp leaf, Injective). Step 5 is evaluation plus naturality of ⊗ and gives the base-change clause. Small cases checked: n=0 (P_0≅A), trivial G, zero ring, i=identity, infinite G. Tool uses accepted as generic: lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison and lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed. That is the universal property of the sheafified free module B[E] on an arbitrary small site; neither assumption states it and it is not a step specific to the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, so it is generic and not a reason to return. It is the only sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality node in the closure.

lean.statement: theorem homogeneous_transpose_extension (J : ActionModule R G) [Injective J.module] (n : ℕ) (H : HomogeneousFunctions R G J n) (N M : ActionModule R G) (i : N ⟶ M) [Mono i] (h : N ⟶ H.object) : Mono ((InternalBar.freePower R G n) ◁ i.val) ∧ ∃ α : InternalBar.freePower R G n ⊗ N.module ⟶ J.module, (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (t : Fin n → C(S, G)) (x : sectionModule R N.module S), InternalBar.onSections R α S (InternalBar.pureTensor R _ _ S (InternalBar.generator R G n S t) x) = homogeneousEvaluate R G J n S ((H.internalHom.hom.val.app (op S)).hom (InternalBar.onSections R h.val S x)) S (𝟙 S) (Fin.cons 1 t)) ∧ (∀ α' : InternalBar.freePower R G n ⊗ N.module ⟶ J.module, (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (t : Fin n → C(S, G)) (x : sectionModule R N.module S), InternalBar.onSections R α' S (InternalBar.pureTensor R _ _ S (InternalBar.generator R G n S t) x) = homogeneousEvaluate R G J n S ((H.internalHom.hom.val.app (op S)).hom (InternalBar.onSections R h.val S x)) S (𝟙 S) (Fin.cons 1 t)) → α' = α) ∧ ∃ β : InternalBar.freePower R G n ⊗ M.module ⟶ J.module, (InternalBar.freePower R G n) ◁ i.val ≫ β = α ∧ ∀ (S T : Profinite.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (t : Fin n → C(T, G)) (x : sectionModule R N.module S), InternalBar.onSections R β T (InternalBar.pureTensor R _ _ T (InternalBar.generator R G n T t) (InternalBar.onSections R i.val T ((N.module.X.obj.map f.op).hom x))) = homogeneousEvaluate R G J n S ((H.internalHom.hom.val.app (op S)).hom (InternalBar.onSections R h.val S x)) T f (Fin.cons 1 t)
